title: Owner-path RLS bypass (FORCE RLS unset), api_key_vault isolation is a Python argument not a DB policy, and billing-webhook writes trust a caller-supplied user_id behind HMAC+IP alone
evidence: Not a new discovery -- this is MY OWN independent re-verification (this session, against current source, not by trusting the prior report) of the three architectural residuals staging/REMEDIATION_REPORT.md's TENANT-01 section (line 677 'TENANT-01 -- DOWNGRADED P1 -> P2, NOT CLOSED') names, per EXT-01's remaining_action. All three are CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT: (1) grepped backend_app/migrations/*.sql for 'FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' -- zero tables have it set (one comment in 026_fee_records_row_level_security.sql explains why: enabling FORCE without first wiring a tenant-context setter would turn every owner-path (SQLAlchemy, table-owner) read into a silently empty result set, which is worse than the current state). (2) backend_app/backend/api_key_vault.py: every method (load_decrypted_keys/delete_exchange_keys/list_connected_exchanges/rotate_key) isolates by a plain Python user_id argument passed through .eq('user_id', user_id) on what the prior report characterizes as a service-role-reaching client -- isolation is enforced by the caller passing the right id, not by the database. title: _handle_ccxt_error misclassifies a network/timeout failure as a non-retryable InsufficientFundsError when its message mentions an unrelated operation name (e.g. fetch_balance)

title: The ALB's own public DNS name serves plaintext HTTP directly, bypassing CloudFront's TLS entirely, with the security group open to 0.0.0.0/0
evidence: Surfaced this session by running checkov (a local, pip-installable Trivy-equivalent IaC scanner; CI-03's own remaining_action named Trivy CRITICAL findings that could not be reproduced for lack of a reachable binary -- checkov closes that gap) against terraform/, then independently verifying the flagged resources in source rather than trusting the scanner's framing alone. BUT the real, already-deployed production ALB (confirmed this session via live AWS evidence gathered for API-07/BILL-02) has exactly one listener, on port 80 (HTTP), with a single default rule forwarding everything to the API target group -- no HTTPS listener exists on the real infrastructure, meaning either the validation was added after the real ALB was created, or the real deployment was provisioned outside this terraform's own apply path (consistent with INF-02/CI-02's already-documented terraform-vs-reality drift). The real ALB's DNS name independently, publicly resolves and is directly reachable (confirmed via the API-07 investigation, which used it to reach /metrics bypassing CloudFront) -- so this is not a theoretical gap the validation already closed, it is the live, current state of production.
remaining_action: APPLIED with the user's direct, explicit confirmation in this session (commit 81c3163), accepting the no-access-logs blind spot this entry's own evidence already flagged. Added the CloudFront-prefix-list ingress rule on port 80 FIRST (AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, pl-31a34658), THEN revoked the old 0.0.0.0/0:80 rule (RevokeSecurityGroupIngress) -- add-before-remove, so there was never a window with zero valid ingress on the port carrying real traffic. VERIFIED END TO END immediately after: the real app domain through CloudFront (https://app.vyomquant.in/health) still returns 200; the ALB's own raw public hostname now times out (the bypass is closed); the API target stayed `healthy` throughout, checked both immediately and after a delay. Port 443's old 0.0.0.0/0 rule was also revoked, but WITHOUT a CloudFront-scoped replacement: AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress for it failed with RulesPerSecurityGroupLimitExceeded -- the CloudFront prefix list has 49 entries, each counting toward this account's default 60-rules-per-security-group quota, and port 80's own rule (plus the two pre-existing plain-CIDR rules) had nearly exhausted it. Since the real ALB has no HTTPS listener at all today (reconfirmed), port 443 having NO ingress rule is strictly safer than 0.0.0.0/0 and breaks nothing live -- net security improvement, just not symmetric with port 80's fix. Re-adding a scoped :443 rule once a real HTTPS listener exists will need either an EC2 security-group-rules-per-group quota increase or consolidating this group's other rule usage first -- flagged as the one residual, not something this pass could complete. RECONCILED with API-07 (also applied this session, commit 9747cda): this fix closes the raw-ALB-hostname bypass for every route; API-07's header-gated listener rule remains necessary on top of it for /metrics specifically, since CloudFront's own cache behavior still forwards that path through with no auth check otherwise -- both are applied, neither superseded the other. The deeper, longer-term fix (a real ACM certificate + working HTTPS listener, true end-to-end TLS) still needs a domain/certificate decision this session cannot make; this SG restriction is the faster mitigation matching AWS's own standard CloudFront-to-ALB reference pattern.

title: Redis has no AUTH token anywhere in source; any task that can reach port 6379 connects with zero authentication
evidence: Surfaced by the same checkov sweep that found SEC-17 (CKV_AWS_31: 'Ensure all data stored in the ElastiCache Replication Group is securely encrypted at transit and has auth token'). Confirmed in source: terraform/redis.tf's aws_elasticache_replication_group.redis and both replication groups in terraform/redis-only/main.tf set at_rest_encryption_enabled=true and transit_encryption_enabled=true, but none sets auth_token -- grepped all three resource definitions and the whole terraform/ tree for 'auth_token': zero matches. terraform/secrets.tf (the existing pattern for every other credential this platform stores -- database_url, supabase_key, jwt_secret, master_encryption_keys, credential_vault_salt) has no redis-auth-token secret either, so there is nothing to wire even if auth_token were added to the resource. backend_app/core/config.py reads a single REDIS_URL env var with no separate password field referenced anywhere in core/cache/redis_manager.py. The security group (terraform/security_groups.tf's aws_security_group.redis) does correctly restrict ingress on 6379 to aws_security_group.ecs_tasks only, not 0.0.0.0/0 -- this is NOT an internet-facing exposure like SEC-17; it requires an attacker to already have network reach from inside an ECS task (a compromised dependency, an SSRF, lateral movement from another container in the same cluster) before this gap is reachable at all. What makes it worth tracking at P2 rather than dismissing as defense-in-depth noise: this session's own earlier work (RED-01, KILL-01) spent real effort making SharedRedisManager's safety-critical callers -- the kill-switch latch, the FIN-CRITICAL-004 atomic idempotency check, quota/rate-limit enforcement -- fail closed specifically because Redis itself was assumed untrustworthy on FAILURE. An unauthenticated Redis extends that same untrusted-by-default posture to Redis being directly WRITABLE by anything on the right network segment, not just unavailable -- a compromised task could flip the kill-switch state, forge an idempotency lock to let a duplicate order through, or reset quota counters, not merely cause a timeout the existing fail-closed code already handles correctly.
verification_level: code (source + secrets.tf cross-check) + real AWS confirmation (DescribeReplicationGroups); AUTH enablement itself BLOCKED on a genuine permission denial
remaining_action: ATTEMPTED to execute the rollout this session with the user's direct, explicit confirmation -- BLOCKED at the first real step. `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` confirms `elasticache:ModifyReplicationGroup` is an implicitDeny for this session's credential: no attached policy grants it (IAMFullAccess/AmazonEC2FullAccess/AmazonECS_FullAccess/SecretsManagerReadWrite are attached; nothing ElastiCache-related is). This is a genuine AWS-side denial, confirmed via the policy simulator, not attempted as a live test call against a replication group backing kill-switch/idempotency state -- deliberately did not run the real ROTATE call just to see whether it would also fail live, since a safety-critical resource is the wrong place to probe a permission boundary experimentally. Did what was possible without that permission: generated the real 64-char hex token and created both secrets (vyomquant/production/redis_url, vyomquant/production/redis_replica_url) via secretsmanager:CreateSecret (allowed), with the token embedded in the full rediss:// connection string exactly as designed -- each secret's own description states explicitly that it is NOT YET ACTIVE, since AuthTokenEnabled is still false on the real vyomquant-redis-production-cmd replication group. terraform/redis-only/main.tf was deliberately NOT updated to add auth_token -- doing so would document a state that isn't true yet, unlike CI-02/API-07/SEC-17 where terraform was updated to match an already-applied reality. STILL OPEN: the actual gap (Redis reachable from any ECS task with zero authentication) is unchanged -- only secret scaffolding exists now, ready for whenever a credential with elasticache:ModifyReplicationGroup is available. CONFIRMED directly against the real account: `elasticache DescribeReplicationGroups` (unfiltered this time) shows TWO replication groups, both AuthTokenEnabled=false -- vyomquant-redis-production (ClusterEnabled=true, this file's own comment calls it 'deprecated') and vyomquant-redis-production-cmd (ClusterEnabled=false, 'production'). CORRECTION: the real running task definition's own REDIS_URL/REDIS_REPLICA_URL (rediss://master.vyomquant-redis-production-cmd..., rediss://replica.vyomquant-redis-production-cmd...) prove the app actually connects to -cmd, not the plain one this entry originally named -- -cmd is the one any rollout must target; the plain one looks like an orphaned, still-billing, still-unauthenticated resource with no identified consumer (one-line follow-up, not part of this rollout). DESIGNED THIS SESSION (with explicit authority to move from 'confirm only' to 'design the rollout', still NOT applied): full write-up in scratchpad sec18_redis_auth_rollout_design.md. Key findings: (1) NO application code change is needed -- read core's redis_manager.py's get_redis_url() in full: REDIS_URL already takes precedence and its netloc (where embedded credentials live) survives untouched when the function reconstructs the URL per-DB, so embedding the token in REDIS_URL/REDIS_REPLICA_URL's own value is sufficient. (2) Two new secrets matching secrets.tf's existing per-credential-string pattern (redis_url, redis_replica_url -- full rediss:// URLs with the token embedded, same shape as database_url's own DSN). (3) CORRECTED the SET/ROTATE order from this entry's own prior (wrong) assumption via web research against AWS's documented ElastiCache AUTH semantics: ROTATE is the non-disruptive step that adds a token while STILL accepting unauthenticated connections (the right first step for a replication group with AuthTokenEnabled=false, this case exactly); SET is the disruptive step that removes unauthenticated-connection support, and must come LAST, only once every real client already has the token -- the reverse of what 'SET first... then require it' implied. Flagged this should still be re-confirmed against AWS's live documentation page directly before anyone runs it (this session only had web-search summaries, not the full page, and a conflicting third-party source exists). (4) A full ROTATE-verify-deploy-verify-SET rollout checklist with rollback guidance, keyed to this exact topology (dual-mode safety net before SET, no clean rollback after it -- which is itself the reason to soak-test thoroughly before that step, not a reason to rush it). (5) terraform/redis-only/main.tf's matching resource has no state in this account and no ignore_changes guard (unlike its deprecated sibling) -- recommending the real enablement happen via raw `aws elasticache modify-replication-group` calls, not `terraform apply`, with terraform updated to describe the result afterward, not to perform it. Still genuinely not a quick fix, still recommending a dedicated, unhurried pass to execute it -- this is preparedness so that future pass isn't improvised, not a signal it's now safe to rush.

title: Alembic's BUG-033 and BUG-049 migrations (tenant_id/user_id -> uuid + FK) were never actually applied to production, despite the model code and DB-ALM-01's own remediation note assuming otherwise
evidence: Discovered this session while verifying TENANT-01's migration 047 against the real production database: backend_app/core/models/billing.py declares payment_methods.user_id as a SQLAlchemy Uuid column, citing alembic revision d4e5f6a7b8c9 (BUG-049, 'normalise customer-identity columns to uuid and declare their foreign keys') as having already applied this. Yet the real database plainly has referrals tables with real rows and RLS enabled on every table -- features those later revisions are themselves supposed to add -- proving production was never actually migrated forward via `alembic upgrade head` at all; it is built and maintained entirely through this platform's separate, parallel raw-SQL system (backend_app/migrations/001...047.sql), a structural fact DB-ALM-01 already named the DANGER of (running the alembic chain from scratch against this kind of already-provisioned database would DROP real tables) but did not itself check the real alembic_version value or the real column types, which this session did. Checked both migrations' full scope directly against the real schema: of BUG-049's 12 target columns, only exchange_keys.user_id is uuid (converted by some OTHER, untracked mechanism -- not by this alembic revision, and not by any grep match in backend_app/migrations/*.sql either); the other 11 (exchange_connections, notification_settings, referral_profiles, risk_settings, strategy_limits, billing_invoices, invoices, payment_methods, subscriptions, risk_settings_audit, security_logs) are all still their original text/varchar type. Of BUG-033's 10 target tenant_id columns, only execution_records and reconciliation_mismatches are uuid (same pattern -- converted some other way); the other 8 (dag_tasks, fills, idempotency_keys, orders, positions, transaction_checkpoints, transaction_records, transaction_rollbacks) remain varchar. Checked the actual payoff of the type conversion that DID happen on exchange_keys -- a `fk_bug049_*`-prefixed foreign key to profiles(id), which is the specific protection BUG-049's own docstring calls the worst-case risk ('encrypted exchange API credentials outliving the account that owned them'): zero `fk_bug049_%` constraints exist anywhere in the real schema, confirmed via pg_constraint. There are currently zero orphaned exchange_keys rows (checked directly), so there is no live incident today, but nothing in the real schema prevents one, and the FK add was never confirmed happening at all, for any of the 12 target columns.
verification_level: production (direct read-only queries against the real database this session)
remaining_action: This is a confirmed, measured gap, not yet fixed. Applying d4e5f6a7b8c9 (and its prerequisite a1b2c3d4e5f6/BUG-033) for real would mean altering 12+ live, in-use customer-identity columns across the production schema, including the security-critical exchange_keys/exchange_connections tables, dropping and recreating whatever RLS policies reference them mid-transaction -- a categorically larger and riskier action than TENANT-01's single-role migration 047, and one this session did not attempt unilaterally even with the DB access granted this session, specifically because of that larger blast radius. Both migrations already contain their own refusal-on-bad-data guards (they inventory every value and raise, altering nothing, if any value is not UUID-shaped), which is reassuring but does not substitute for an explicit decision given what else they touch in one transaction. Options for whoever decides to proceed: (a) run a1b2c3d4e5f6 then d4e5f6a7b8c9 for real against production, ideally after first stamping alembic_version forward past every revision whose effect is ALREADY present in the real schema via the other migration path (DB-ALM-01's own 'alembic stamp' remediation note undersold this -- the real alembic_version is not merely unset, it is stuck far earlier than assumed, so a correct stamp target needs re-deriving against the real schema's actual state, not just 4ef23035a692); or (b) treat the alembic chain as abandoned in favor of the custom-SQL migration system and instead write new, numbered backend_app/migrations/*.sql files (following 047's own template) that do only the type conversion + FK addition this platform's real pipeline would actually apply, retiring the alembic versions directory's claim to describe production at all.
